scope: Additional read-only governance-boundary assessment; no rule/source edits or model calls
decision: Current model invocation is not demonstrably governed and must be corrected before enabling it. A tightly scoped model data-selection step can remain ordinary host implementation work; neither read-only mode nor an independent label creates an exemption or a new admission.

finding.problem: Before model execution the launcher checks only that CURRENT_FRAMEWORK.json exists. It then assigns a dedicated independent configuration Agent role, explicitly excludes repository instructions, disables automatic rules, and supplies no verified Yuanheng/foundation/current host mandate context or existing agent admission. No inventory allowlist or tools-disabled sandbox establishes that missing governance chain. The function output is later used to configure and activate host runtimes, so it is not merely an inert test transcript.
finding.classification: Definite governance-context/enforcement gap. The present code is insufficient to attest either an admitted independent Agent or a governed step of the existing operator host. The evidence does not itself require registering a new Agent definition: the function is one structured data selection with no native tools, framework identity or independent publish/permission authority. Do not infer a blanket exemption; remediate and review the exact implementation as a host step.

evidence.meaning: Tools-disabled, temporary and external model steps cannot assert that governance does not apply.

No exemption; host owns identity/mandate/state; context contains shared core/template/frozen foundation/current responsibility/actual mandate. Ordinary business code does not require a new definition pass. Trust comes from a host-trusted baseline, not merely matching a nearby JSON lock.

Frozen invariant explicitly covers temporary, derived, external and third-party instances. Unmanaged instances cannot participate as GongGong Agents, obtain tool permission or submit effective results.
Model-driven steps retain governance, actual mandate/resource/budget limits, context and task/attempt receipts. Tools disabled does not eliminate call consumption or reconciliation duties.

Only Agent/skill definition generation, new versions and external definition integration invoke definition review. Ordinary authorized code repair and use of existing capability do not require newly fabricated review passes or future-candidate admission.

Default sources are core.md, yuanheng Agent template, FOUNDATION.md and host-issued task mandate. Registered IDs are yanshi/kuafu/diting/heqi/sinan; no codex-runtime-config identity exists. Their current manifest admission paths are pending records, so borrowing a name/pass would not be valid.

Normal loader verifies package integrity, exact candidate/admission and reporting, then assembles shared context plus mandate. It invokes Python for integrity; simply calling it would reintroduce the missing-Python bootstrap dependency.

scope=offline_registered_snapshot_consistency_only, exemption=null, registration_note says byte integrity is not approval. This provides file hashes for consistency, not a general bootstrap authorization.

Historical host record explicitly says it does not create or approve a new Agent. Existing user authority covers automatic configuration and repairing GitHub/runtime setup, not a permanent governance exception.

minimal_authorized_correction: Keep this as a bounded structured selection step under the existing authenticated editor/operator host. Remove the instruction that rejects repository instructions and remove claims of a separately admitted independent Agent. The prompt should explicitly retain Yuanheng/foundation governance and say only the broken requirements/Issue/Python bridge dependency is bypassed for environment repair; permission and activation remain exclusively with the existing host.

Before any provider invocation, use PowerShell/.NET to load and verify the relevant current governance context from a host-trusted installed/source baseline: resolve CURRENT_FRAMEWORK with its declared path base, reject absolute/traversal/link escapes, verify current pointer/manifest and selected core/template/foundation/AGENTS/GOVERNANCE bytes against the already trusted host release snapshot. Verify foundation.lock consistency too, but do not accept a lock or frozen-distribution file supplied by the same untrusted workspace as the sole trust root. The trusted release/snapshot hash must be supplied or pinned by the existing authenticated host boundary. Do not silently select a mutable workspace governance root or a stopped old candidate.

Attach the verified shared core, template, complete frozen foundation, relevant host policy and the actual host-issued scope/authority/operation identity as prompt context. Inventory remains a delimited untrusted data section. Missing Python/Node does not prevent this: Get-Content -Encoding UTF8 / File.ReadAllText with UTF8, ConvertFrom-Json, Get-FileHash or SHA256, and .NET path/reparse checks suffice. No new governance rule or rewritten foundation is needed.

Keep tools disabled, exact selected-path allowlisting, source_runtime forbidden and host-only deployment. Bind actual selected CLI/model and a bounded single-call attempt to the existing setup operation; persist attempted/completed/failed-or-unknown before/after the call and retain any unavailable usage as unknown. Use the existing responsibility/receipt chain when Python is repaired; do not equate a local log with Diting delivery or automatic production admission.

Fail closed only for the model-selection/activation step if the host cannot establish its governance trust or actual mandate. Continue discovery, diagnostics and other already authorized independent work. A deterministic host selection/explicit local path repair can restore missing runtimes without making an ungoverned provider call. This is a scoped fallback, not an exemption.

--ignore-rules can only remain if its narrow purpose is preventing untrusted workspace/config auto-loading and the complete required trusted policy/mandate is explicitly injected. Removing that flag alone is insufficient because the current working directory may be mutable/untrusted and it does not prove admission or trust. No need to automatically load every repository/framework file.

If implementation instead retains a separately accountable independent Agent definition or grants it autonomous tool/resource/publish authority, stop that newly introduced capability and follow existing gonggong-check / exact definition admission and reporting before enablement. This conditional is not a demand to create such a definition or obtain redundant user approval for the scoped host correction.
recommended_targeted_validation: Native mock consumes UTF8 stdin and asserts core/template/full foundation and exact host mandate appear once, before the untrusted inventory; non-ASCII paths survive.
Corrupt governance source, pointer path-base/traversal, reparse destination, or trusted-snapshot mismatch: provider mock invocation count remains zero; no activation.
Mutating both a workspace policy and its colocated lock/snapshot cannot confer trust.
Missing Python/Node still allows the PowerShell governance precheck/context assembly and controlled selection fixture; no production bridge/Issue intake dependency is introduced.
No implicit reuse of pending Agent pass, model-proposed identity/permission or arbitrary source_runtime; retain original tools-disabled tests and exact allowlist rejection.
Unknown/interrupted provider attempt is retained and requires actual reconciliation/explicit scoped retry rather than an automatic second charge; unavailable usage remains unknown.
